doc.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Meeting Mongo Santamaria
summary: Mongo and Candido come from different Havana neighbourhoods and met when a friend recommended him as tres player; they remain lifelong friends.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, let us go back to the group Septeto El Apolo. You made mention several times of Mongo Santamaria, who of course was a percussionist of your era very well known here in the United States with a very long history. How did you and Mongo meet? Did you grow up in the same neighborhood?

No, no, no, no. Mongo is from the neighborhood of Jesus Maria and I'm from the neighborhood of El Cerro. Because Havana has forty-three neighborhoods. So, Mongo belongs to the Jesus Maria neighborhood and I belong to the neighborhood of El Cerro. But we met

because someone was looking for a tres player and Mongo was with the Boloña Septet. So they were looking for a tres player and a friend of Mongo said he knew a very good tres player in El Cerro. Then my friend took me to meet Mongo and there began the friendship between us. At that time, Mongo was working for the postal service as I said before and I helped him to deliver the mail so he would finish his work early so that we could start rehearsing really early. That was how our friendship was and is until now, until now. Right now I think they are going to do a tribute to him soon and I was the first to say, "I’ll be the first to be there," because his health isn’t too good now.
Then so long as it deals with Mongo of course - we are friends from childhood. A very good, very good companion, very good companion.
